emma_support: Heads-up — enterprise customer 'FoldOps' reported mismatched tool_result associations when using parallel tool calls via our multi-tool wrapper. They say outputs are swapped between tools ~20-30% of the time. Repro steps below and request_id: rq_0a7f9c

emma_support: Repro steps
1) Send a single API call with two tool calls in parallel using our `multi_tool_use.parallel` helper
2) Observe response: tool_result for `fetch_user_profile` contains the payload from `generate_markdown`
3) Happens intermittently, seems correlated with high QPS

emma_support: Example request/payload:
```json
POST /v1/invoke
{
  "model": "redwood-large",
  "input": "Create summary and fetch profile",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "fetch_user_profile",
      "args": {"user_id":"user_123"}
    },
    {
      "name": "generate_markdown",
      "args": {"title":"Weekly update"}
    }
  ],
  "mode": "parallel",
  "correlation_id": "corr-42"
}
```

emma_support: Attached truncated logs and request id. Customer is blocked; they saw billing anomalies because duplicate tools were billed.

raj_eng: Thanks emma. Assigning. Can you paste the raw response body for rq_0a7f9c? Also which SDK and SDK version? Any middleware that rewrites tool names?

emma_support: SDK: node v3.1.2, no middleware. Raw response (redacted):
```json
{
  "choices": [
    {"tool": "fetch_user_profile", "tool_result": "# Weekly update\n..."},
    {"tool": "generate_markdown", "tool_result": "{\"name\":\"Alice\",\"id\":\"user_123\"}"}
  ]
}
```

sara_infra: Noted. We rolled out batching change to the tool router 3h ago that changes ordering of tool fanout to favor latency (round-robin shards). Rolling back to confirm.

deploy_bot: Deploy 2026-03-16T18:10:12 to tool-router service succeeded (rev f3c2b9). Notify #eng-runtime if rollback needed.

mike_devex: Repro script please — I'll try locally with `--parallel` stress test. Also pls include correlation header if possible.

emma_support: Repro script (minimal) — run this curl loop 100x:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"...","tools":[{"name":"fetch_user_profile","args":{"user_id":"user_123"}},{"name":"generate_markdown","args":{"title":"Weekly update"}}],"mode":"parallel","correlation_id":"corr-42"}'
```

olivia_cs: Customer impacted: missed summaries + doubled billing for some runs. They want ETA and mitigation.

raj_eng: Immediate mitigation: set `mode: sequential` or add `request_meta.correlation_id` on caller side. Long term: sara, can you confirm whether tool_result tagging uses request-scoped monotonic ids or per-call UUIDs? If routing batches reuse slots we may be mapping indices incorrectly.

sara_infra: Investigating: router already tags each worker call with `call_index` but there was a recent optimization that reorders calls post-merge. Potential bug: merged results array not being re-associated by `call_id` when responses arrive out-of-order. Rolling patch now.

alertbot: Incident severity: high — multiple customers reporting data skew in tool outputs. Paging eng-runtime.

raj_eng: Thanks. Emma — I'll follow up with patch PR and timeline. For customer: recommend flip to sequential + add short-term credits. @olivia_cs can you coordinate compensation?

olivia_cs: On it, will propose credits for the impacted runs and update FoldOps.

emma_support: thx all. I'll update customer with sequential workaround and the correlation_id tip. Please post PR link when available.

raj_eng: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tool-router/pull/489 — includes fix to associate by `call_id` and adds extra assertion in unit tests. Deploying hotfix to canary now.

deploy_bot: Canary deploy started for tool-router rev f3c2b9+hotfix (canary 3/20) 2026-03-16T19:02:01

emma_support: FoldOps confirmed sequential mode stops the issue. Waiting on canary results.

sara_infra: Canary looks clean after 1h of load tests, rolling to prod in 15m.

raj_eng: Closing once prod rollback window passes. Good catch, emma. :clap:
